executiveSummary: Multiple government advisories warn of active targeting of PLCs and HMIs in critical sectors. Iranian-affiliated actors have manipulated PLC logic across Water/Wastewater and Energy; immediate removal of direct internet exposure and logic validation is advised Security Advisory . Separate U.S. advisories highlight active reconnaissance and capability development against Siemens S7 PLCs (AI-assisted scripting, S7comm over TCP/102). Prioritize segmentation, access protection levels, and S7 traffic monitoring Security Advisory . Pro-Russia hacktivists continue opportunistic attacks via exposed VNC on internet-facing HMIs, causing loss of view and nuisance changes in WWS and other sectors. Eliminate public VNC and enforce MFA on remote access immediately Security Advisory . Actively exploited MikroTik RouterOS vulnerabilities enable unauthenticated SSH access and device takeover; exploitation observed with rogue admin accounts. Patch to current fixed releases and restrict management planes to VPN/jump hosts only View Advisory . Critical NetScaler ADC/Gateway SAML RCE (public PoC) and Cisco FMC root compromise are being exploited to tamper firewall/VPN policies. Patch/hotfix immediately, restrict exposure, and hunt for webshells and unauthorized policy changes Security Advisory View Article . OT-relevant product flaws demand urgent attention: Danfoss iC7 drives (unsigned firmware/code paths), Eclipse Milo (OPC UA server issues), and SATCOM iDirect iQ terminals (auth/CSRF/info exposure). Segment, apply vendor updates, and enforce signed firmware where supported CISA Bulletin CISA Bulletin ICS Advisory . Browser/Windows exploit kit reuse (Chrome V8 + ALPC LPE) by multiple China-nexus clusters underscores the need to accelerate KEV-aligned patch cycles and enforce enterprise browser extension controls View Article .

relevance: - Direct OT impact: PLC logic manipulation (Rockwell/Schneider/Siemens), HMI loss of view via exposed VNC, VFD unsigned firmware paths, OPC UA server weaknesses (Eclipse Milo). - OT-adjacent risk: SATCOM terminal flaws (iDirect iQ), perimeter device compromises (NetScaler, Cisco FMC, MikroTik) enabling enterprise-to-OT pivot. - Enterprise ingress vectors likely to cascade into OT: Zimbra mail exploitation, PaperCut KEVs, Chrome/Windows exploit chains.

descriptions: Exploitation of public-facing apps (T1190): NetScaler SAML RCE; Cisco FMC root
Valid accounts / default creds (T1078): VNC/HMI, SNMPv1/2 community strings
Living off the land (T1059/T1047): PowerShell/WMI; PLC project edits via native tools
Protocol abuse: S7comm (TCP/102), CIP/EtherNet-IP (44818/2222), Modbus/TCP (502), OPC UA
Web shells and persistence on appliances (T1505)
Data exfil via DNS/HTTPS and cloud storage (Zimbra ops; T1041/T1567)
Ransomware movement (Gunra): Impacket lateral movement, AD credential access
Unsigned firmware/code on OT devices enabling sabotage paths

outlook72h: Expect continued scanning and exploitation attempts against MikroTik routers and NetScaler ADC/Gateway, opportunistic brute-force on exposed VNC/HMI services, and reuse of browser/Windows exploit chains. Heightened risk of lateral movement from compromised edge devices into enterprise AD, then to OT jump hosts. Validate segmentation, block unneeded east-west traffic, and increase monitoring on OT protocol gateways and engineering workstations.
